findings.title: Migration crashes when the `embed_category` site setting row does not exist
findings.body: The migration does `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']`. `embed_category` defaulted to '' and is only persisted in `site_settings` if an admin changed it, so on the vast majority of installs this query returns zero rows and `result[0]` is nil/out of range, raising before the data migration can run. The whole `rake db:migrate` then fails and the deploy is blocked. The row lookup needs to be guarded (e.g. fetch into a variable and check for presence) before dereferencing.

findings.title: Fallback query also dereferences a possibly-missing site_settings row
findings.body: `execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value']` assumes the `uncategorized_category_id` setting is stored in the database. It is a hidden setting with default -1 and is frequently absent from `site_settings`, so this raises in the same way as the `embed_category` lookup. Even when present it can be -1, which would be inserted into `embeddable_hosts.category_id` (declared NOT NULL but with no FK), producing rows that point at a non-existent category.

findings.title: Migrated hosts keep their scheme and are interpolated unescaped into SQL
findings.body: Existing values of the `embeddable_hosts` setting were allowed to be of the form `http://discourse.org` (the old `allows_embeddable_host?` stripped the scheme at comparison time). This INSERT stores the raw line, so after upgrading, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` — which compares `lower(host)` with `URI(referer).host` (`discourse.org`) — will never match those rows and embedding silently breaks for previously-working sites. The value is also interpolated directly into the SQL string, so a stray apostrophe or trailing \r in the setting breaks or corrupts the statement. Normalize each host (strip scheme/path/whitespace, downcase) and bind/quote the value.

findings.title: `create_table ... force: true` can silently drop an existing table
findings.body: `force: true` issues a DROP TABLE IF EXISTS before creating `embeddable_hosts`. If the migration is ever re-run, or if a table with that name already exists (e.g. created by a plugin or a partially applied migration), all existing embeddable host configuration is destroyed without warning. `force: true` should not be used in a schema migration.

findings.title: No index or uniqueness constraint on embeddable_hosts.host
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` runs `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` on every `embed/comments` and `embed/count` request as well as in TopicRetriever, but the table has no index on `host` (and `lower(host)` would need a functional index anyway), so every embed request does a sequential scan. There is also no unique index or model-level uniqueness validation, so the admin UI happily creates duplicate rows for the same host, after which `record_for_host` returns an arbitrary one and the "post to category" mapping becomes non-deterministic.

findings.title: before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil
findings.body: `self.host.sub!(...)` is called unconditionally in `before_validation`. `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` directly, so a create/update request with a missing or null `host` (trivially reachable from the new admin UI or any API client) raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil` and returns a 500 instead of the intended validation error. Guard the callback with `return if host.blank?`.

findings.title: Host lookup compares lower(host) against a non-downcased value
findings.body: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases the stored column but not the value extracted from the URI. `URI#host` preserves the case of the referer/embed URL, so a referer like `http://EvilTrout.com/post` (or a host saved with any uppercase letters) will not match an existing record and embedding is rejected with 'invalid referer host'. Hostnames are case-insensitive; the parameter must be downcased (`host.downcase`).

findings.title: update/destroy blow up with 500 when the id does not exist
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return nil; `update` then passes nil into `save_host` (which calls `host.host = ...`) and `destroy` calls `host.destroy` on nil. Both raise NoMethodError and return a 500 for a request referencing an already-deleted or bogus id — for example two admins deleting the same host, or a stale browser tab. Use `find_by` plus an explicit 404/`raise Discourse::NotFound`.

findings.title: has_many uses `embed: :ids` without `include: true`, so hosts are never sent
findings.body: With ActiveModel::Serializers `embed: :ids` and no `include: true`, the payload contains only `embeddable_host_ids` and no top-level `embeddable_hosts` collection. The client's `store._hydrateEmbedded` resolves `*_ids` by looking up `root['embeddable_hosts']`; when that collection is absent `_lookupSubType` returns undefined for each id, so `embedding.embeddable_hosts` becomes an array of `undefined` and the admin Embedding page renders empty rows. Either sideload the objects (`embed: :ids, include: true`) or embed objects directly.

findings.title: `*_ids` hydration crashes on null and silently produces undefined entries
findings.body: In `_hydrateEmbedded` the new plural branch calls `obj[k].map(...)` without checking that the value is an array, so a serializer sending `"foo_ids": null` throws a TypeError and the whole hydration (and therefore the find/findAll promise) fails. Additionally, when `_lookupSubType` cannot resolve an id (collection not sideloaded) it returns `undefined`, and those `undefined` values are pushed into the resulting array instead of being filtered out; the `hydrated || []` fallback is dead code since `map` always returns an array. Guard for non-array values and compact the results.

findings.title: PUT /admin/customize/embedding ignores its payload and saves nothing
findings.body: `update` only re-renders the freshly built OpenStruct; it never reads `params` or persists anything. The matching client code (`admin-embedding.js.es6` `saveChanges` calling `embedding.update({})`) therefore does nothing either. Either implement the update or remove the route/action and the dead `saveChanges` action so callers aren't misled into believing changes were saved.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents were swapped
findings.body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now defines the `:embeddable_host` fabricator while the new `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` defines `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category` and `:private_category`. This inverts the file-name convention Fabrication (and every other fabricator in the suite) relies on, breaks name-based lookup/lazy loading, and makes the definitions impossible to find. The two file bodies should be exchanged.

findings.title: New write endpoints have no behavioural or authorization tests
findings.body: The only assertion is that the class inherits from Admin::AdminController. There is no coverage for create/update/destroy (including the uncategorized-category fallback, invalid host validation errors, and missing-id handling, which currently 500s), nor for the fact that non-staff/non-admin users must be rejected from these new state-changing admin routes. Given this PR introduces a new writable admin resource, request specs for success, validation failure and access control are needed.

findings.title: Test named "is false if embeddable_host is blank" no longer tests that condition
findings.body: `Topic#expandable_first_post?` no longer consults embeddable hosts at all, so this example passes merely because `embed_truncate` defaults to false and `has_topic_embed?` is false for an unsaved topic. The name is now misleading and the example asserts nothing about hosts; it should be renamed/removed so future readers aren't misled about what behaviour is covered.

findings.title: Underscore-to-dash conversion only replaces the first underscore
findings.body: `type.replace('_', '-')` with a string pattern replaces a single occurrence, so a type such as `some_embeddable_host` would become `some-embeddable_host` and fail the ADMIN_MODELS lookup, silently routing the request to the non-admin base path. Use `/_/g` (or `Ember.String.dasherize`) so all underscores are converted.
